inline:The target never identifies evidence within a single evaluation that would distinguish a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that merely tracks the right answer.
The problem requires identifying what evidence within a single evaluation distinguishes genuine reliability gain from mere compliance that happens to track the right answer. The target describes a mechanism and counterconditions, but contains no such distinguishing evidence: it lacks premises and derivation (both empty arrays), its counterconditions are only observation-evaluated (checker_spec: null), and its text frames compliance purely as a scaling hazard rather than specifying a within-evaluation evidential marker (e.g., item-level process-vs-answer consistency or matched wrong-answer patterns) that separates real reliability from coincidental correctness.
